claim: Dao, Nguyen, Truong, and Hoang define an (alpha, omega)-sensitivity measure for an offline-MBO surrogate as the probability that a Gaussian perturbation of the surrogate's own parameters changes its average prediction by more than a threshold alpha.
stance_target: existence of a weight-space fragility diagnostic distinct from every input-space covariate already eliminated in the offline-MBO paper's seven controls
scope_conditions: Model-agnostic definition applicable to any parameterized surrogate g(x; phi) trained on offline data D
quoted_support: "The (alpha, omega)-sensitivity of a model g(x; phi) on the offline dataset D is defined as S_phi(alpha, omega) := Pr_{gamma~N(omega_mu, omega_sigma^2 I)}[A(phi, gamma) >= alpha], where A(phi, gamma) := E_{x~D}[g(x; phi+gamma)] - E_{x~D}[g(x; phi)]"

claim: High (alpha, omega)-sensitivity implies there exists a neighborhood of input at which the surrogate's prediction is brittle against small perturbations of its own parameters.
stance_target: the interpretability of the sensitivity measure as a fragility diagnostic usable at a specific query point (e.g. a candidate optimum)
scope_conditions: Follows from Lemma 3.2 of the paper, given S_phi(alpha, omega) >= 1 - delta
quoted_support: "Suppose S_phi(alpha,omega) >= 1-delta with delta in (0,1). Then, with probability at least 1-delta over the space of random perturbation gamma, there exists x in D such that |g(x;phi+gamma) - g(x;phi)| >= alpha"

claim: The paper's proposed regularizer only ever reduces surrogate sensitivity and is demonstrated exclusively on neural-network surrogates; it runs no experiment applying the sensitivity measure to, or manipulating the sensitivity of, a Gaussian process.
stance_target: scope limitation: the sensitivity measure itself is reusable as a post-hoc diagnostic on any surrogate, even though this paper's own regularizer application is neural-network-only and one-directional
scope_conditions: Confirmed via full-text search: the paper's only Gaussian process mention is a bibliography citation to an unrelated third-party paper on GP kernel-choice robustness
quoted_support: "This raises the following questions: (1) how to regulate the sensitivity of a surrogate model; and (2) whether conditioning an offline optimizer with such less sensitive surrogate will lead to better optimization performance."
